title: Apple Music Event London (2004) FULL
speaker: Steve Jobs
content:
Good morning.

Thank you.
Thank you all for coming.
Um, well, we're here to talk about iTunes today, clearly.
And, uh, for those of you that have never used it, uh, iTunes is the best music jukebox in the world.
And, uh, if you've lived in the US, it's been the best online music store in the world.
And we're pleased to report today that we've sold over 85 million songs that have been sold and downloaded, uh, online, setting a new record.
So we're within striking distance of 100 million songs.
It's amazing.
And this is in just a little over one year.
Uh, the iTunes music store has a 70% market share of all legal downloads.
70%.
But that's only been interesting if you've lived in the US until today.
Because today we're introducing the iTunes music store into the UK, Germany, and France.
Now, these three countries represent over 60% of current European music sales.
62%.
And they represent 23% of global music sales.
So this is a, a, a huge chunk of the global music sales.
UK, Germany, and France.
Now, before we show you the store, uh, or the stores, uh, I want to go back to the beginning and talk about the philosophy behind iTunes.
Uh, and there's no better place to start than who does iTunes really compete with?
Now, in the US, you might say it's Napster, Rhapsody, and Music Match.
Uh, over here in Europe, you might say it's OD2 and Virgin.
But this isn't really true because iTunes has a 70% market share.
All the rest of these guys put together, you know, are 30%.
It's not really who iTunes competes with.
Who iTunes really competes with is this.
It's piracy.
This is the big market for downloads.
And if you don't think it's so big, take a look at this.
This is what the piracy, this is how piracy has impacted the music market in these countries.
It's brought it to its knees in the UK with zero growth last year.
But that's phenomenal compared to what it's done in Germany and France.
The market shrunk in Germany by 19% and it shrunk in France by 14%.
So piracy is a really big market and this is our competitor.
So if you're going to compete with piracy, you have to understand it and you have to offer a better product.
And that's what we've tried to do.
So let's understand piracy first.
When you go, how many of you have downloaded a song illegally?
Go ahead.
I tried it.
Yeah, because I market research.
And, uh, what I found was you get really unreliable downloads.
You search for a song.
You don't just find one song.
You find 200 copies of that one song.
And some people say they have a really fast interconnection.
You go to download the song and you find out they fibbed.
So the song downloads really slow.
The next one craps out halfway through.
And you have to try several times before you actually get the song.
But when you finally get the song, you find that it was encoded by a 10-year-old and the last four seconds is cut off.
So you have to start the whole process over again.
So you have very unreliable downloads and you have very unreliable encoding.
You also don't get previews of the song.
So you might have wasted all this time downloading the wrong song or the wrong version of the song.
And you don't get album cover art, which everybody would like to have.
And maybe most of all, it's stealing, right?
It is stealing.
So, what are we going to do about this?
How are we going to offer a better product?
Well, the first thing we're going to do is replace unreliable downloads with fast, reliable downloads coming off of our giant server farms.
We're really good at this.
We give very fast, very reliable downloads.
Next, we're going to replace unreliable encoding with perfect encoding.
We encode everything ourselves.
We check everything.
Uh, it's, it's great.
Very high quality, pristine encoding.
No previews, we're going to replace with previews of every song in the store, free 30-second previews, and they're in high fidelity.
They're in the same quality as the downloads.
So you don't have to listen to previews that are much lower quality like other people do.
Obviously, we're going to give you great album cover art and it's not stealing.
It's good karma.
So this is, this is the basis for fighting piracy.
Now, we're going to combine this with landmark personal use rights.
And so what are we going to let you do with the music?
Well, first of all, you own it.
There are no subscription fees.
The experiment's been run.
People don't want to rent their music.
They want to own it.
They bought cassette tapes, they bought CDs, they want to buy downloads.
If you, you know, your favorite song, you listen to a thousand times in your life.
If I, I'm going to be listening to my favorite song in 10 years.
If I have to pay 7, 8, 9, 10 pounds a month to listen to my favorite song, after a year, I mean after 10 years, that's a, that's over 1,000 pounds to listen to my favorite song.
And I don't want to do that.
I want to buy it.
I want to own it for all time.
I don't want anyone to tell me I can't listen to it 10 years from now if I stop, stop paying a subscription fee.
So in iTunes, you own the music.
There are no subscription fees.
Unlimited CD burning.
You can burn your favorite track on any number of CDs.
We put a limit on how many times you can burn a single playlist, which is seven, which is anywhere from two to four more than anyone else gives you.
But each track, you can burn an unlimited number of times.
So you can always have your favorite song on every CD you burn.
You can play your music on up to five computers.
This is two more than we started with.
And you can mix and match, match Macs and PCs.
You can have all PCs, all Macs, or any combination in between.
And an unlimited number of iPods.
CD burning is getting less important as people have iPods.
They can put their music on their iPods in unlimited number for personal use.
So, again, you own the music, no subscription fees.
Unlimited CD burning for personal use.
Burn any playlist up to seven times.
An unlimited number of iPods and you can play it on up to five computers, PC and Mac.
And this, this last point's key.
You can authorize and deauthorize your computers.
So if you've got your music on five computers and you want to get rid of one, donate it to your school and buy a new one, let's say, you can deauthorize that one you're going to donate and free up a slot and authorize the new computer.
So as you grow and migrate from computer to computer, your music can follow you.
So these are landmark personal use rights.
And it's taken more than a little negotiation, uh, with us and the labels to arrive at, I think, a great set of personal use rights that customers are responding very positive to.
They really are the gold standard of personal use rights in the, uh, legal online business.
We combine this with some great features.
We're the only folks to offer one-click downloading.
You click buy song or buy album and it begins the download instantly, charges your credit card, does the whole thing.
One click.
Very, very easy.
And we integrate iTunes right into the world's best jukebox.
This is really important.
Some people believe that you can sell music online with a website.
No can do.
Website music stores suck.
If any of you've used them, they, they don't really work.
And some people have thought they could write an application which was different than the jukebox.
So you buy your music in one application and then you have to get it into the jukebox and it's not very nice.
We've integrated it right into the jukebox.
Here's the iTunes music store.
You just flip, select one of the playlists, you're right in the jukebox.
You buy a song, it goes right into a purchase music, uh, album or a playlist and you can just go find it right there.
It's integrated right into the best jukebox in the world.
It's also Mac and PC.
Run it on your PCs all you want.

And, uh, if that's not a definition of irony for you, I don't know what it is.
But it's a phenomenal app on Mac and on Windows.

Moby, Dave Brubeck, you know, Pete Rock, a lot of these in there and more coming every day.

We've recently added a whole new section on music videos.
So we got lots of music videos now.
And we've got them, you know, people like Coldplay, Jet, Snow Patrol.

I've got this one in video here just to show you.
This is what it looks like.
Quality's great.
I'm all at sea.

Forgot my roots.
If only for a day.
So that gives you a feeling for the quality.

Welcome to sessions at AOL.
I got a kind of woman.
Do anything in this world for me.
So you get the feel for what the music videos are like.
And again, these are all free.
You can just go on and watch them.
So music videos.
And last, we've got something really cool that we just added called iMix.
And what iMix is is it's a chance for you to put together your celebrity playlist if you will for yourself and post it on iTunes.
And so you can make your album with as many songs as you want in it.
Click a button, it uploads it to iTunes where everyone can take a look at it.
Your identity is never revealed, uh, but you get to write a little, uh, write a little note about it and this is what people see.
And so, you know, you, you can write a little note to tell them what it's like.
It builds a composite album cover out of the covers of the albums of the tracks that you've selected, shows all the tracks and lets people listen to them, preview them for free and buy them if they want.
But it also lets people rate them.
And so people can rate these things and you can see which are the top rated ones and go to them and check them out.
We've had over in, in, in the, in the, in the, let's see, less than 60 days since we, uh, turned on iMix, we've had over 50,000 people post iMixes and over 100,000 people vote.
So here's a great one, you know, 60s gold.
Somebody likes 60s music.
My favorite though is this one, the worst music on iTunes.
Somebody went through and found, uh, what they thought was the worst music on iTunes, put it together in a playlist and, you know, these things have, have been pretty popular.
And again, you can see them rated up here, you know, four stars, four stars, some are rated four and a half, occasionally a five-star one.
Um, and you can go check them all out.
And it's pretty cool.
So all of these things together and what we've done to make a better product than piracy has made iTunes what it is today.
And today we're bringing it to the UK, Germany, and France.
And we're bringing it across the pond with 700,000 tracks available for download and purchase.
And these tracks are from all the five major labels plus dozens of independents and we're signing up more independents day by day.
And as you can imagine, they want their music on the most popular online music store in the world.
We also have over 12,000 classical tracks from labels like Deutsche Grammophon, EMI, Decca, a whole bunch of them.
And we have a bunch of exclusive tracks.
Again, we get the best exclusive tracks because we have the biggest audience and people want, uh, want their tracks to be heard.
So, let's take a look at each of these stores.
First, let's start with the UK.
Each of these stores is programmed with local content, so they're a little bit different.
This is the UK store.
Again, obviously in English and every song on the UK store is going to be available for download and purchase for 79 pence.

We think these prices are going to excite a whole lot of people.
